purpose: Tralokinumab-ldrm is used to treat moderate-to-severe eczema (also called atopic dermatitis) in adults and children 12 years and older when other treatments have not worked well enough. It helps reduce the itching, redness, and rash that come with eczema. It is often used along with a steroid cream applied to the skin.
how_it_works: Your immune system makes a protein called IL-13, which plays a big role in causing the inflammation and skin irritation seen in eczema. Tralokinumab-ldrm is a lab-made antibody that specifically blocks IL-13, preventing it from triggering that irritation. By blocking this signal, the medication helps calm down your immune system's overreaction and allows your skin to heal.
common_side_effects: Upper respiratory infections (like a cold), eye irritation or redness (conjunctivitis), injection site reactions such as redness or soreness where the shot is given, and cold sores (herpes simplex).
warnings: Tell your doctor if you have any eye problems, since eye irritation is common and may need treatment. Let your doctor know about any infections before starting this medication. Do not get live vaccines while using this medication. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before using it. Stop use and contact your doctor right away if you have signs of a serious allergic reaction such as swelling, trouble breathing, or rash.
typical_dosing: Adults and teens 12 and older usually start with two injections given under the skin (one in each thigh or abdomen) as the first dose, then one injection every two weeks after that. Your doctor may adjust this schedule based on how well you respond. Each injection is given just under the skin, and your doctor or nurse will teach you how to do it yourself at home.
